title: Ja'afar the Barmecide and the Old Badawi

full_text:
Ja'afar the Barmecide, while riding through the desert outside Baghdad with a company of courtiers, met an elderly Bedouin riding a shaggy camel, carrying a hunting falcon upon his wrist and a patched leather waterskin across his saddle.

Desiring to enjoy the legendary wit of the desert nomads, Ja'afar halted his steed and called out: 'From whence come you, O father of the desert?'

The old Bedouin looked down from his saddle and replied with calm dignity: 'From the vast earth of heaven, young master.'

Ja'afar smiled: 'And whither are you traveling?'

'Whither my camel carries me and destiny directs my steps,' answered the Bedouin.

Ja'afar chuckled: 'And what is the name of your famous tribe?'

'A tribe that feeds the guest in famine, strikes down the oppressor in battle, and holds its head higher than the mountain crags!' replied the nomad proudly.

Ja'afar, delighted by his fearless answers, took off his gold signet ring and said: 'If you can tell me three things that are identical, three that are opposites, and three that never change, I shall give you this ring of gold and a hundred dinars.'

The old Bedouin answered without a moment's pause:
'Three things are identical: the breath of the desert, the soul of a free man, and the flight of an arrow.
Three things are opposites: truth and falsehood, light and darkness, the generous hand and the clenched fist.
And three things never change: the turning of the heavens, the debt of mortality, and the honor of a noble heart!'

Ja'afar was enchanted by the depth and poetic elegance of the nomad's words. He handed him the gold ring, ordered a hundred gold dinars to be weighed into his saddlebags, and invited him to his palace in Baghdad.

The Bedouin thanked him with royal courtesy, rode into the sunset, leaving Ja'afar to reflect that wisdom dwells not in palaces, but in the open sands where freedom sharpens the mind.
moral: Desert wit, poetic pride, and quick banter earn the admiration and generosity of princes.
